questions.q: Missing a deadline in an airbag controller is an example of which type of deadline?
questions.explain: A missed hard deadline means system failure that may cause harm.

questions.q: Under rate monotonic scheduling, which task gets the highest priority?
questions.explain: RMS gives fixed priorities by rate: shorter period means higher priority.

questions.q: Three tasks have $(C,T)$ of $(1,4)$, $(2,6)$ and $(1,10)$ ms. What is the total utilisation $U$? Give 3 decimal places.
What is the Liu and Layland utilisation bound for $n = 2$ tasks? Give 3 decimal places.
On a single processor with $D_i = T_i$, EDF can schedule a task set if and only if:
questions.explain: EDF is optimal on one processor, so any set with $U \le 1$ is schedulable.

questions.q: Which technique lets a low-priority task holding a lock temporarily run at the priority of the highest task waiting for it?
questions.explain: Priority inheritance bounds the blocking time caused by priority inversion.

questions.q: An emergency stop button with a known minimum time between presses and a hard deadline is a:
questions.explain: Sporadic tasks are irregular but have a minimum inter-arrival time and a hard deadline.

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the four necessary conditions for deadlock?
questions.explain: The condition is *no* pre-emption. Allowing pre-emption breaks deadlock.
